Ashford plans a congestion toll on the Riverside Bridge. Drivers and shop owners are furious; transit riders and cycling groups cheer.

On Monday the “Ashford City Council” published a plan to charge 6 dollars for every car crossing the “Riverside Bridge” at peak hours from next March. “Dana Whitfield”, deputy mayor for transport, said the toll would fund forty new buses and cut queues on the bridge by a third. “Marcus Lowe”, head of the “Ashford Transit Authority”, promised buses every six minutes on the bridge route.

“Frank Doyle”, chair of the “Ashford Motorists League”, called the toll “a tax on working families” and said the league will collect signatures to block it. “Rosa Mendez”, who runs a bakery on Bridge Street and speaks for the “Bridge Street Traders Association”, said her customers already struggle to park and the toll would empty the street. “Tom Kerrigan”, a delivery driver quoted by the “Ashford Evening Post”, said he would lose a day's pay each week.

“Priya Shah” of “Cycle Ashford” said the plan is overdue and asked the council to add a protected bike lane. “Leo Grant”, a professor of urban economics at “Ashford Polytechnic”, said tolls in comparable cities cut traffic by 15 to 20 percent, but warned that low-income commuters need discounts. “Nina Okafor”, a nurse who takes the bus across the bridge, said a faster bus would change her mornings.

“Gavin Price”, a councillor from the “Northside Ward”, said he will vote against the plan unless residents get an exemption. “Ellen Brooks”, editor of the “Ashford Evening Post”, wrote that the council has not shown how the money will be ring-fenced. A council vote is set for next month.
